def: An event in which an AI system's behaviour causes or nearly causes harm or a serious breach of expectations, whether or not anything is technically down.
A switch built in advance, such as a prompt rollback or a kill switch, that reduces what an AI system can do during an incident.
An ordered set of containment levers, from least to most capability given up, of which on-call picks the lowest that stops the harm.
The most drastic containment lever, which turns an AI feature off and hands the work to people.
The incident rule of doing the safe, reversible thing that stops the harm first and investigating the cause afterwards.
An incident or malfunction of a high-risk AI system that leads to defined kinds of serious harm, which providers must report to authorities within set deadlines.
A judge or rule that scores a sample of live traffic so that quality can be monitored and alerted on.
A review that asks what in the system allowed an incident, not who erred, and ends in tracked changes.
